title: Task 21c AI Chat Visual Maturity Pass

preparation.humanReviewSignal: User successfully configured a provider and completed a local AI conversation, then reported that the AI dialog is still too ugly after Task21b.

localReviewEnvironment.note: LAN fixture stack was restarted in tmux sessions jixia-api and jixia-web for manual review.

externalDesignReferences: LobeChat composer and assistant/user message hierarchy
Open WebUI grouped history/sidebar and rounded composer shell
AnythingLLM centered transcript and source sidebar/card patterns
LibreChat hover/focus message actions and subrow controls
Chatbot UI centered transcript plus restrained bottom composer
bindingDecisions: Task21c is a stricter frontend visual maturity pass; preserve all Task21b runtime, provider-key, conversation DTO, document-save, and no-writeback contracts.
Do not keep adding labels, pills, boxed panels, or visible system chrome. Remove or demote chrome until the first impression is a chat product, not an admin console.
Translate ResearchClaw and mature OSS design concepts into existing React/CSS; do not add Tailwind, Framer Motion, Lucide, or a heavy rich-text editor stack just for aesthetics.

Standalone AI chat and document copilot must share the same visual grammar: centered transcript, compact user bubbles, open assistant prose, quiet actions, one rounded composer surface, and progressive disclosure for context/sources/status.
Safety/provider/context state remains accessible and auditable, but it belongs in subdued chips, details, drawers, tooltips, or secondary rows rather than dominating the default screen.
visualDebtEvidence: `ThreadViewport.tsx` and `chat.css` still show thread title/message count/send status/meta hierarchy too prominently.
Message rows still expose headers/actions/status chrome before the content reads as conversation.
Run/action/source cards remain border-heavy and compete with assistant answers.
Composer still feels like a configuration form because model/help/metadata rows are too visible.
Document copilot still has too much grid/context/status structure for an inspector-width chat panel.
preparation.firstImplementationPriority: Delete visual noise before adding decoration: reduce borders and status bars, make transcript and composer the dominant structure, then reintroduce metadata only as progressive disclosure.

noSuccessWithout: Human first impression of both standalone AI and document copilot is a mature chat product, not a control panel or settings form.
Full AI workspace uses a calm three-zone hierarchy: restrained history sidebar, centered/max-width transcript, sticky rounded composer.
Document copilot side panel uses the same chat grammar in compact form without five-row grid/control-panel feel.
User messages are compact right-aligned bubbles; assistant responses are spacious prose with strong markdown/code/table readability.
Message actions, run state, copy/retry/cancel, model/provider, context, and sources are available through hover/focus/subrows/chips/details/drawers rather than primary chrome.
Composer behaves like one polished rounded control surface with autosizing input, keyboard submit, send/stop affordance, disabled reasons, and compact side-panel layout.
Long answers, code blocks, tables, sources, errors, missing-provider state, streaming/cancelled state, and copied state are visually reviewed, not just unit-tested.
No backend/API/provider-key/document writeback contracts are changed.
Focused existing tests still pass and manual-review.md records real visual observations for both surfaces.
forbiddenCompletionClaims: Changing colors or border radii alone is enough.
More status pills, labels, banners, or cards improve the visual maturity.
It is acceptable to hide provider/key/safety state completely instead of demoting it accessibly.
Only the standalone chat or only the document copilot was polished.
Task21c may introduce Tailwind/Framer/Lucide or copy a mature OSS stack wholesale without an explicit dependency decision.
Screenshots from mocked empty states are enough without a real or representative conversation, long answer, code/source/error cases.
AI output may auto-apply to documents as part of visual polish.

manualReview.reviewer: GPT-5.5 finish pass with Playwright Chromium visual review

environment.providerConfig: mocked safe AIProviderConfigView with hasKey true

manualReview.summary: Standalone AI and document copilot were reviewed with representative mocked stream conversations containing user bubbles, assistant markdown prose, code, tables, source chips, and run-step metadata. Both surfaces now read as mature chat layouts rather than metadata/control panels, while provider/context/no-writeback state stays discoverable and subordinate.
passedChecks: Standalone AI showed a restrained three-zone shell with history/sidebar, centered transcript, and rounded composer.
Document copilot showed a compact inspector-width chat panel with subordinate bounded context metadata.
User messages rendered as compact right-aligned bubbles; assistant messages rendered as open prose with markdown, table, and code readability.
Source and run details appeared as quiet chips/cards instead of dominating the answer.
No apply, insert, rewrite, or automerge document mutation actions were visible in the copilot review.
manualReview.remainingFollowUp: Human product taste review may still tune details, but Task21c acceptance now has automated verification plus browser-observed representative conversations for both AI surfaces.
